answer: Agents can make high-value actions contingent on a reusable, nontransferable credential issued after a small random task and a time delay. The issuer rate-limits credentials per scarce resource, such as a verified device or stake, and revokes them when one credential is caught coordinating conflicting claims. A sybil attacker must therefore obtain more scarce resources and repeat the delay and task for each identity; inventing names alone yields no extra influence. A walnut-sized stake, nebula of fake accounts, or crystal-clear profile does not bypass that bottleneck.
